Wrote `spec.md` and `acceptance.md` at the repo root (replacing the previous task's, per this pipeline's convention).

**What the intent maps onto, after reading the code:**

1. **"change the color of the tag"** — genuinely impossible today. Colour is set once at creation, and `createTag` (`server/bridza-store.js:387`) early-returns the existing entry when the slugged name already exists, ignoring the colour passed in — so retyping the name with a new swatch is a no-op. The only workaround is a duplicate tag under a different name. Spec adds `updateTag` (store → `POST /api/bridza/tag/update` → client) and makes each tag row's dot in the kanban picker expand the existing swatch row.

2. **"tags should be displayed on the … detail page"** — one judgment call worth flagging: the **task detail page already renders chips** in its topbar (`src/app/features/task.jsx:364`). The place a task appears *without* its tags is the **plan board** — `plan.jsx:116` builds its task model and drops `t.tags`, so neither the node nor the side panel shows them. Since the intent names the plan board explicitly ("the tag that I have for card on the plan board or kanban"), I scoped this half to the plan board: colour dots on the node, full chips in the panel. If you actually meant something else by "tags detail page" — a registry/settings screen listing all tags — that's not in the spec and would need one more line of intent.

Explicitly out of scope (not asked for): renaming tags, deleting tags, editing the palette, and a tag picker on the plan board.

The plan-board node is the one constrained bit: a default node is 50px tall with the title line holding the `~Nh` estimate, the bottom edge holding the progress bar, and the corner holding the resize handle — so the spec puts dots right-aligned on the sub-text line, capped at 4 with all names in the tooltip, and acceptance has a criterion for that collision.

**Fit check:** this is a single feature — one store function, one endpoint, a picker interaction, and a display addition on the plan board. It stays in the "Feature" flow; no `flow-fit.md` needed.

## Implemented

**Store** — `updateTag(root, { id, color })` in `server/bridza-store.js:405`, beside `createTag`: rejects a colour outside `TAG_PALETTE` (`invalid color`) and an unknown id, otherwise sets `refs.tags[id].color`, writes `refs.json` and commits it as `bridza: recolor tag "<name>" (<id>) → <color>`. `refs.taskTags` is never touched.

**Bridge / client** — `POST /api/bridza/tag/update` (`server/bridge.js:300`), `api.updateTag` (`src/app/api/client.js:40`).

**Picker** (`TagMenu`, `src/app/features/board.jsx:33`) — each tag row's dot is now its own button next to the name button; clicking it expands that tag's eight swatches (one row at a time, current colour marked `on`). A swatch collapses the row, calls `updateTag`, and fires the board's `onChange` so chips repaint from the reloaded registry. The name still toggles assignment; the "new tag…" row is unchanged.

**Plan board** (`src/app/features/plan.jsx`) — `tags` carried into the task model; up to four dots right-aligned on the sub-text line (`cy=33`, ending at `nw-16` so they clear the 12px resize corner at any node height), with a `<title>` naming every tag; full `.tag-chips` in the task side panel under the pipeline/state line. No new CSS — the circles carry `tag tag-<colour>` to pick up the existing palette `color`.

**Tests** — `updateTag`'s three outcomes with a real refs round-trip plus a clean `git status` (`bridza-store.test.js`), and the recolour flow in the picker: dot click reveals swatches, a second dot replaces the open row, a swatch calls `updateTag`, `setTaskTags` is never called, row collapses (`board-tags.test.jsx`).

## Verification

`pnpm lint` and `pnpm build` pass. Test suite: **294 passed, 1 failed** — the failure is `create-pr.test.js > falls back with the compose URL when gh is not on PATH`, which sets `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` expecting `gh` to be absent there; on this machine `gh` is in `/usr/bin`, so the call reaches GitHub and returns a different error. Pre-existing and environment-dependent — it touches `server/bridza-run.js`, which this change does not modify.

I ran the suite against a symlinked `node_modules` from the main checkout (the worktree has none) and removed the symlink and `dist/` afterwards; the working tree holds only the seven changed source files.

`review.md` is written. Summary:

**Verdict: approve with fixes.** The implementation matches the spec closely, adds no dependency/abstraction/CSS, and reuses the existing palette classes. `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build` are clean; the two touched test files pass (69 tests).

**Merge into `main`: clean.** `git merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD` exits 0 with a tree and no conflicts. Nothing in the branch's outputs names a landing branch other than `main`.

Findings against acceptance.md:

- **F1 (real acceptance failure, reproduced)** — `updateTag` uses a truthiness check on `refs.tags[id]`, so `id: "constructor"` returns `{ ok: true }`, writes `{"constructor":{"color":"cyan"}}` into `refs.json`, and commits `bridza: recolor tag "Object" (constructor) → cyan`. The criterion says an unknown id must change nothing on disk. One-line `hasOwnProperty` guard.
- **F2** — plan-board dots likely overlap the sub-text at the 170px minimum node width with 2+ tags (arithmetic, not a measured render).
- **F3** — the `<title>` sits on the inner `<g>` of four 3.5px circles, so tag names only appear when hovering a dot, not the node as the criterion words it.
- **F4** — at the 38px minimum node height the dots cross the progress bar, which the criterion names explicitly for the resized case.
- **F5** — cosmetic: the dot lost `.item`'s 9px padding and its hover fill.

Over-engineering — three small deletions, nothing structural: drop the `Math.min(t.tags.length, 4)` that re-derives `slice(0,4)`'s length; `updateTag`'s `{ ok, id, color }` echo is never read by its one caller; the three inline style props on the dot button belong in one CSS rule.

Two notes on the environment: the one `pnpm test` failure (`create-pr.test.js`, "gh is not on PATH") is pre-existing — that file is untouched by the diff and the same test fails on `main`, because a real `gh` is installed here. And the root `review.md` is a shared file that each review stage overwrites — the copy I replaced was task #111's review, still available at `git show HEAD:review.md`.
